title: The anti-American Right
gist: Texas GOP Railroad Commission nominee Bo French's anti-Indian tweet about UT football fans exposed a split between establishment Republicans (Cornyn, Cruz, Rove) and a New Right base that treats group competition as zero-sum. Smith argues this coalition-shrinking instinct makes the New Right a loud but numerically weak fringe, and that a moderate pro-immigration position is winnable for Democrats.

themes.theme: Bo French firestorm and GOP split

insights.claim: Bo French, the GOP nominee for Texas Railroad Commissioner who trails his Democratic opponent in polls, set off a national firestorm with an anti-Indian tweet about University of Texas football fans that drew about 47M views.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The Texas Railroad Commission regulates oil and gas; a competitive race for the seat is worth watching for energy-sector regulatory continuity.

insights.claim: Establishment Texas Republicans including John Cornyn, Ted Cruz, Jared Patterson, Lacey Hull and Dustin Burrows denounced French's tweet, Karl Rove said he would vote for the Democrat, while Governor Greg Abbott, who endorsed French, offered only mild criticism.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Visible intra-GOP fracture in Texas raises odds of Democratic upsets in down-ballot statewide races.

insights.claim: Despite official condemnations, Republican tweets denouncing French were heavily attacked on X and right-wing media figures rallied to French, indicating the GOP base leans toward the New Right over the establishment.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Signals the direction of Republican primary electorates and future party positioning on immigration.
insights.quote: it’s easy to tell which way the wind is blowing among the GOP base

themes.theme: Zero-sum worldview of the New Right

insights.claim: Smith argues the New Right treats nonwhite immigrants and their children as adversaries regardless of legal status, skill level, assimilation, crime rates or party affiliation, so no pro-immigration argument can persuade it.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Policy debates on high-skilled immigration (e.g. visas for tech talent) will not be settled by economic evidence within this faction.

insights.speaker: Noah Smith

insights.claim: After Trump's 2024 win brought Hispanic, Asian and some Black voters toward Republicans, the New Right squandered the opening through racially profiled deportations, anti-Muslim 'civilizational' framing and tolerance of Nazi apologetics, and is now alienating Indian Americans, a group about as numerous as Jews and higher-earning.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Reversal of 2024 minority voter shifts would raise Democratic odds in upcoming elections and change policy outlook.
insights.locator: The New Right had a golden opportunity

insights.claim: Smith contrasts the New Right with 1970s-80s Christian conservatives, who won by bringing Catholics, white ethnics and some Jews in as 'co-belligerents', arguing the inability to build alliances will ultimately doom the New Right.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Coalition breadth is a leading indicator of a political movement's durability.

insights.claim: Gallup polling shows 73% of Americans say immigration is a good thing versus 21% who do not, implying the New Right is a loud fringe that relies on online aggression to mask numerical weakness.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Mainstream opinion supports continued legal immigration, limiting the political durability of hard restrictionism.

insights.claim: Trump is now underwater on immigration, 52% to 47% per NYT polling, which Smith views as a slim margin Democrats can widen.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Immigration has shifted from a Republican strength to a liability, relevant to midterm forecasting.
insights.locator: Indeed, the tide may already be turning

insights.claim: Smith recommends Democrats adopt a moderate liberal immigration stance that respects the law and treats immigration as a privilege, and make common cause with restriction-minded but non-xenophobic Republicans like Cornyn rather than answering maximalism with maximalism.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A centrist Democratic immigration pivot would improve their electoral odds; watch party messaging.
insights.locator: That means the immigration argument is winnable
